adapters.says: Claude Code's command-line runtime starts one non-interactive agent turn per invocation: `claude -p <prompt>` runs the prompt to completion in the working directory it was started in, `--output-format json` makes its standard output one JSON document carrying the result and the run's own accounting, and `--permission-mode acceptEdits` lets that turn write files without a human answering a prompt it has no way to show. The turn ends when the agent stops; a non-zero exit means the turn did not complete. Taken from the product's command-line documentation as the orchestrator knew it at its 2026-05 knowledge cutoff, and NOT measured on this machine by this declaration: no run of this adapter has been observed by the dispatch port, so every sentence above is a CLAIM and the adapter is honest rather than green. What C3 measures: that the binary is present and authenticated, that the flags are spelled as written here, that the JSON document's shape is what an orchestrator can read an artifact out of, and that a worker started this way is visible in the orchestrating runtime's own agent panel (ADR-017 decision 8) -- which is an adapter concern and never the architecture. What this adapter deliberately does NOT declare, now that the round-trip EXISTS in the port (ADR-017 slice C4): `asks` and `resumes`. The port will carry a worker's question back and an operator's answer in, and it does so through two declarations this row would have to make -- the exit code this product uses for 'I need input', and a declared channel its question and its way back in come out of. Neither has been measured on this machine, and neither is documented as a distinct ending: `-p` runs one turn to completion and a non-zero exit means it did not complete, which is silent about the difference between a turn that failed and a turn that needed an answer. Declaring an exit code here would be this kit inventing a protocol for somebody else's product and then reading its own invention back as a fact. So a worker started through this adapter cannot reach `input-required`, and that is an honest absence rather than a broken round-trip: the first measured run of this product is what will either supply those two declarations or confirm that this intelligence must be resumed some other way. Route options: the model, effort and (where the product has one) spend cap a route cell declares are passed as --model, --effort, --max-budget-usd -- flags read from the installed product's own --help on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.301, codex-cli 0.154.0), 2026-10-16. A turn cap has no flag here, so the port's wall-time stop condition is the cap every product honours.
